title: Elementary Statistics for Social Sciences II
text:
Preface
This book covers the first half of 208272 Elementary Statistics for Social Sciences II: the principles of statistical inference, inference about means, proportions and variances, and analysis of variance. All examples use economic contexts. Unless a source is given, the numbers in the examples are hypothetical and are used for illustration only.

title: Elementary Statistics for Social Sciences II
text:
Notation for critical values
The subscript of a critical value is the area to its left. This is the same convention as the R functions qnorm(), qt(), qchisq() and qf().








Notation
Meaning
R




\(z_{0.975}\)
the \(z\) value with area 0.975 to its left
qnorm(0.975)


\(t_{0.975,\,24}\)
the \(t\) value with 24 df and area 0.975 to its left
qt(0.975, 24)


\(\chi^2_{0.025,\,10}\)
the \(\chi^2\) value with 10 df and area 0.025 to its left
qchisq(0.025, 10)


\(F_{0.975,\,5,\,8}\)
the \(F\) value with (5, 8) df and area 0.975 to its left
qf(0.975, 5, 8)



A value calculated from the sample has the subscript “cal”, for example \(z_{\text{cal}}\), \(t_{\text{cal}}\), \(\chi^2_{\text{cal}}\) and \(F_{\text{cal}}\).

title: Elementary Statistics for Social Sciences II
section: The five steps of a hypothesis test
text:
The five steps of a hypothesis test

Hypotheses: state \(H_0\) and \(H_1\).
Level of significance: state \(\alpha\).
Test statistic: write the formula, substitute the values, and give the result.
Critical value and critical region.
Decision and interpretation.

title: Elementary Statistics for Social Sciences II
text:
Writing the conclusion
Decision using the critical region (Chapters 1–2 and Section 3.1)

\(t_{\text{cal}}\) = … [falls / does not fall] in the critical region (\(t_{\text{cal}}\) [<, >] …), so we [reject / do not reject] \(H_0\).

Decision using the p-value (from Section 3.2 onward)

p-value = … [<, \(\ge\)] \(\alpha\) = 0.05, so we [reject / do not reject] \(H_0\).

Interpretation

That is, … at the 0.05 level of significance.


If we reject \(H_0\), write \(H_1\) as a sentence.
If we do not reject \(H_0\), write \(H_0\) as a sentence.
For a two-sided test that rejects \(H_0\), also state the direction, using the sample statistic.

Confidence interval

We are 95% confident that … is between … and ….
